steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Stir in pasta and return to a boil. Cook, stirring occasionally, until cooked through but still firm to the bite, about 13 minutes; drain.

Meanwhile, heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion, orange pepper, and garlic; cook and stir until tender, about 5 minutes. Stir in Italian sausage; cook and stir until browned and cooked through, about 8 minutes. Stir in undrained tomatoes and heavy cream; reduce heat to medium-low and cook 5 minutes more.
Mix pasta into sauce; stir in the Parmesan cheese and garnish with fresh parsley.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheesy Sausage Pasta
raw_recipe.description: This deliciously cheesy sausage pasta dish has a rich and creamy tomato-based sauce — it might just become your favorite macaroni recipe!

review.reviewBody: This can be very good, but I have to say that 16 oz. of pasta is way too much here and the sauce needed a bit of work. I used half the amount of pasta (basically half a box of penne). I sauteed 1/2 cup of vidallia onion in 1 tbsp. of olive oil along with garlic. I used more than a tsp. and left out the bell pepper because I didn't have any on hand. I used two 14.5 oz. cans of seasoned diced tomatoes and one 6 oz. can of tomatoe paste to give it some thickness. I added some additional dried seasonings (basil, oregano, italian seasoning) to taste along with 1/4 tsp. of red pepper flakes. I fried the sausage (crumbled out of the casing) separately and added that to the sauce to avoid any greasiness. I let that simmer for about an hour and added the cup of heavy cream at the end and let that simmer on low. I served this over the pasta, garnished with fresh parsley and topped with grated parmesan vs. adding the cheese to the sauce.

Agree with an earlier commenter Jillian that 16 oz pasta is too much and 8-12 oz is much better. I also made some of her other changes such as the 2 cans of diced tomatoes which works better than stewed due to short cooking time, added 1 tsp Italian seasoning and 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, crumbled the sausage (I didn't fry separately though as I liked/wanted the grease/flavor). I also added 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella to the dish, along with the 1 cup parmesan to make it extra cheesy.

I added some fresh basil, oregano and since I doubled it I used 1 lb mild Italian. sausage and 1 lb hot italian sausage. I also browned it separate from the veggies and then combined. Used small rigatoni. It was delicious . Pleased my large Italian family yesterday (Sunday dinner). Great change from traditional Sunday meal. Complimented with home made bread, stuffed artichokes and Ceaser salad!!!

My kids loved this and it was quick and easy to make on a busy night. I used more onion (probably 1/2c), 2 cloves of garlic, chicken sausage removed from the casings, wide egg noodles and 1/2&1/2 instead of cream. I cooked the sausage separately to avoid the extra grease going into the sauce. After thickening the sauce, I let it rest for a few minutes before pouring it on the pasta. This is definitely a keeper!

Delicious!!!! Hubby loved it! I made it according to the recipe except a few parts... I used 1/4 of an onion, 2 cloves of garlic, a green bell pepper, 1 1/4 cup of parmisan, 1/2 cup of mozzarella, and I chopped up the stewed tomatos :) I also like a thicker sauce so I stirred in a desperate bowl 1/2 a teaspoon of cornstarch and a teaspoon of water and added it to the sauce while simmering. Turned out great! I will be making this again!

Quick, tasty and simple! I used half the amount of pasta, skipped the oil and bell pepper and subbed diced tomatoes with garlic instead of the stewed with separate garlic. So good and so easy - thanks for this recipe!

This recipe' is so good I've made it several times. The only problem I have is that just 1 can of stewed tomatoes is not enough sauce to even begin to cover the shells, Even with the heavy cream. I use 2 cans of stewed tomatoes and add a small can of tomato paste with about 1/2 can of water from paste can. I always add a little sugar when I use paste because paste tends to be bitter. This makes the correct amount of sauce to cover the shells. This is a delicious recipe' that I will continue to make over and over !!!!

Well received in my household! I doubled the recipe by doubling all the ingredients except the pasta - kept that at 16 ounces. I used 1 pound of Italian sausge and one pound of Bob Evans orginal sausage. I also did drain the sausage after cooking it - a must. Also, I did use freshly grated Parmesan cheese - not the prepackaged stuff.
This is definitely a keeper. I added celery to the peppers onions and garlic. Bleneded w half of the tomatoes and pinch of oregano and thyme.
My husband and I both loved this dish. I did add red pepper flakes and used about 1/4 cup of onion. I also added a dash of oregano. Delicious with a little kick! Will definitely make this again!

The cream sauce is great. I added my own spices - basil, pepper, red pepper flakes and oregano. I added diced instead of stewed tomatoes. My sauce simmered on the stove for a while as I waited for my husband to get home from work. End result was awesome!

This recipe is delicious! My son loved it. I used chicken Italian sausage and replaced the Parmesan cheese with Swiss cheese because I'm not crazy about Parmesan. It has great flavor with the orange pepper and tomatoes. I will definitely make this a regular.
Loved it!
One of the best meals. About a #4 difficulty. Well worth it.
This was delicious! Very easy to make and it hit the spot!
Excellent. Just need to add a little more stewed tomatos.

Delicious! I used wide noodles instead though, so next time I need to use less pasta. I also added a little basil and pepper, otherwise made it exactly as the recipe said. Family all seemed to like it, so I'm happy! It was a last minute decision. I knew I wanted to use sausage and pasta but didn't know what else. I searched for a recipe with those ingredients and found this recipe. Love this website!
Very good. I increased the garlic and cheese. Used half the pasta and half & half instead of the cream.

I made it pretty much true to the recipe, except I didn’t have heavy cream, so I used a little milk and some Velveeta cheese. I also thought the dish looked like it could use some spice, so I added Cajun spices and Cayenne pepper. We were pleased with the results, but agreed that it might have been better with 1/2 the sausage (perhaps medallions) plus some chicken. Regardless, one of the things I liked about the recipe was how easy it was to adapt the portion size. There’s only two of us and we don’t love tons of leftovers, so I appreciated that I was able to create just enough for a meal. And it was quick and super easy.
Fantastic! I added some sliced mushrooms and a lot more garlic, plus some Italian seasoning to the meat. Also used more parmesan than was called for. Will definitely make it again!
